plugins.name: phased-execution
plugins.description: Run large work as a dependency graph of right-sized Claude sessions — plans, per-phase handoffs, and a computed ready-set. Ships a zero-dependency local web console: one install serves every project, each repository getting its own console, port, state and supervisor from a single `cd <project> && phase-console start` — list them, open one by name, and drive any of them with the same verbs. Its autopilot heals its own runs: a halt an agent can clear launches a bounded recovery session by itself, and when the board reads fixed the run record moves with it and carries on, so one press either finishes the plan or parks it on something only a person can do, named. Gates are categorized by who can clear them: an ai gate is the booted session's first task (verify the conditions, do the work, record the clearance, continue) while a human gate carries numbered operator steps beside an Approve button on the phase page — one approval clears a gate of any kind and can resume the run it parked. Register many Claude accounts and watch their real usage meters — a run switches accounts at a limit, or waits out the window and resumes itself. Name the MCP servers a plan needs and the console proves them before a run spends anything: a server that was never signed in is found at boarding rather than an hour in, and by default the phase runs without it and records what it could not do, instead of one signed-out server halting a plan that never asked for it. A plan or a single phase can insist its servers are required and park instead; either way, signing one in requeues everything waiting on it. A session now declares how it ended rather than leaving the runner to read prose: a phase waiting on an external clock — a CI image build, a deploy window, a PR merging itself — parks with its window and its watch refs and resumes its own session when the window elapses, a lock another plan holds queues behind the named holder instead of parking forever, and a record the board has already overtaken closes itself instead of being re-run. Plus scope-aware concurrency so disjoint plans run at once while intersecting phases queue, per-session freeze/continue/stop, closable plans that stop reporting work nobody will do, per-session tabs, remaining-time estimates, a plan-mode wizard that drafts a plan before writing it, and Tailscale onboarding to drive it all from your phone. The console also installs prebuilt via npm (phase-console) or Homebrew (zsarir/homebrew-tap/phase-console). v2.2.0 reorganises recovery into one model: every stuck run or phase shows its 'Ways forward' — the phase's own session resumed, a fresh briefed agent, re-check, retry — each button carrying exactly what will happen, on every page including the fleet and the phone. The runner stops failing phases over missing binaries (a §Verification command whose tool this machine lacks is skipped and recorded, with lint warning at plan time), a blocked handoff is reported as blocked instead of 'no handoff written', a halt the board has already moved past retracts its urgent notification, and the whole console is usable one-thumb: the software keyboard no longer hides the terminal, scrolling works everywhere, tables become cards. v2.2.1 adds the Pulse — the plan page and a new #/pulse page lead with which phases are being worked on this second, in what vehicle, on what model, with ticking elapsed clocks, plus what is queued behind which lock and what is parked waiting on the world with its wake-up countdown — one Recover & continue button per stopped plan (re-read the board, stand down what it already settled, heal a real halt through the same bounded auto-recovery, name what needs a person), one-click re-run of a failed verification command in the integrated terminal with the exit reflected back onto the phase, and a phone terminal that actually works: live Esc/Ctrl/arrow keys, touch scrollback, and an 80-column floor that pans sideways instead of wrapping TUIs into confetti. v2.3.0 makes the autopilot converge by itself: a stopped phase is classified from evidence (never started, work in progress, done but unrecorded, verification red, declared blocked, a resource wall, a stale or live foreign claim, a manual gate) and its situation's ladder is climbed — its own session first, a fresh briefed session next, an account or model switch at a wall, one bounded unblock session on a declared blocker — never the same rung twice, bounded in rungs and dollars per phase, run and day; a convergence loop runs it at boot, on a docs change, every few minutes, a minute after any stop and on Recover & continue, releases the lock debris of dead runs and ended sessions, and resumes the lanes a console restart killed; when the ladder is spent the phase carries one errand (what is needed, how to give it, what was tried) and the run drives everything else. Every Ways forward shows the situation, the rungs tried and the next rung; the dashboard's Waiting on you lists only errands, permission cards and sign-ins; the Pulse shows each plan's last convergence pass; Settings ▸ Automation grew the ladder's caps and toggles. A session-presence hook lets the console see every Claude session in its repository: a hand-run claude shows on the Pulse, its lock is a queue while it lives and debris the moment it ends, and its declared outcomes drive the same machinery as a lane's.
